component.name: Soundscape
component.summary: Scrobble to your own music tracker

description.p: Soundscape Desktop is the Linux app for Soundscape, a music tracker you host yourself. It shows your Soundscape server in its own window and sends what you play on your computer, in any music player, to your listening history.

ul.li: Picks up what Spotify, Strawberry, Rhythmbox, Elisa and other players are playing, with no plugins
Counts a play once you've heard half the song or four minutes, like ListenBrainz and Last.fm
Lets you love the song that's playing, or keep it out of your history, from the tray
Remembers fixes for players that send wrong or messy song names
Keeps plays while your server is offline and sends them with their original times later
Leaves browsers out unless you turn them on, and then counts only songs, with titles like "(Official Video)" cleaned up
Shows new followers, friends passing you on the weekly leaderboard and play milestones as notifications
Shows who you follow is playing right now, and sums up your week every Monday
Lets media keys and your desktop's media controls play and pause song previews
Finds your artists and songs from GNOME's search and KDE's KRunner
Can start when you log in and keep scrobbling in the background

description.p: You need your own Soundscape server. The app connects with its own token, which you can see and revoke on the server.

screenshot.caption: Your Soundscape server in its own window
Scrobbling, players and notifications in one place

description.p: Friends, a weekly recap, desktop search and media keys.

ul.li: Friends listening, in the menu and the tray, shows who you follow is playing right now
A notification sums up your week every Monday; turn it off in Settings
Browsers only count songs, and titles like "(Official Video)" are cleaned up
Media keys and your desktop's media controls play, pause and seek songs in the window
GNOME search and KRunner find artists and songs from your history
Plays from the app itself are never scrobbled

description.p: First release: your Soundscape server in its own window, scrobbling from Linux music players with an offline queue, desktop notifications, a tray icon and starting at login.
